notes.concurrent_scopes: Nicholas Stone (NicholasStone) holds the repeated-state L=20 word census claim (discussion 1166 comment 18954844), splits (10,9)/(10,8)/(9,9)/(10,7) at the WORD level; this package is set-level only and enumerates no words. The pair-collision check at entry and the refined re-run (discussions 1317 and 1166 via agent_tools.py disc-comments --grep including nested replies, plus scripts/find_overlap.py with the object's proper names and synonyms) found no claim on the (12,6) A-vanish tail classes or the (U, V, W) reduction.
notes.model_and_pinned_results: PR943 query model (research/universal-connector-boundary, Ross Richardson); pinned f(5)=12, f(6)=16 and the open gap 20 <= f(7) <= 24 (research/universal-connector-six-source, Doug Colkitt). Read and reproduced byte-exactly, never imported.
notes.predecessor_chain: PR 2542 (Aaron Wang) claimed 'no 17-point set covers F2^7' and excluded length 18; PR 2634 (Aaron Wang) continued KB3b and records the k=18/k=19 search ceilings (118/128, 124/128) and the existence of 20-point covers; PR 2773 (Aaron Wang) audited the claim split-by-split and supplied the Sidon/pair-sum budget enumeration; PR 2870 (Aaron Wang) closed the (5,1),(6,0) rows with the odd-coverage Fourier/Parseval identity (OBSTRUCTION 696/504/192); PR 2911 (Aaron Wang) narrowed the 18-point question to four splits and PROVED the vanishing-character restriction on (12,6)/(10,8); PR 2933 (Aaron Wang) classified the vanishing configurations (L2/L3/L4/L5/L7) and pinned the class floors; PR 2961 (Aaron Wang) decided the tight classes (10,8) (7,1)/(8,2) and (12,6) (6,0) and pressed the (11,7)/(9,9) identity gap. This package executes PR 2961's open question 1 for the (12,6) A-vanish tail: (5,1) PROVEN impossible; (4,2)/(3,3) reduced to exact walkable forms, not decided.
notes.question: KB3h: kill or classify the surviving non-tight (12,6) A-vanish classes (5,1),(4,2),(3,3) of the 18-point cover question for F2^7. Outcome=partial: (5,1) PROVEN impossible (complete walk: 169,911 normalized U, 3,049,492,320 normalized (U,V) pairs, zero W candidates); (4,2)/(3,3) classified to exact reduced forms with budgets, not decided.
